title: Musk Weighs In on Memory: Praises Micron's Future Pricing, Slams "Extortionate" Practices
key_facts: In an X post on 14 Oct 2026 Elon Musk said Micron "has been reasonable regarding future memory prices, while others have been extortionate" and that such treatment is something customers "won't forget".
Money Today reports the remarks sparked speculation that he meant Samsung Electronics and SK hynix; Musk named neither and gave no details of price talks.
In July Musk thanked Micron for "making room for Tesla in the years to come" despite "pretty insane" market prices (Investing.com transcript).
Micron had 26 long-term supply agreements by September, up from 16 in June (FUTUBULL); Reuters puts their value at USD 32 billion, up from USD 22 billion in June, mostly backed by cash deposits.
Citing JPMorgan, Money Today says Micron's long-term commitments could cover more than 75% of its fiscal 2027 production.
Hankyung reports Samsung has secured agreements covering nearly 80% of its 2027 memory output, including HBM; The Elec says SK hynix has roughly five-year agreements with more than 10 customers.
quote_evidence: In an October 14 post on X, Musk singled out Micron for praise, saying the U.S. memory giant “has been reasonable regarding future memory prices, while others have been extortionate.”
However, he did not explicitly name either company or disclose details of any pricing negotiations.
Reuters further reports that the total value of these commitments had climbed to $32 billion from $22 billion in June, with most backed by cash deposits.
why_it_matters_hint: A major buyer is publicly rewarding one memory supplier and warning others as memory prices stay high.
notes: TrendForce compiles reports from several Korean and international outlets; the target of Musk's remark is speculation by Money Today. Musk's own post was not opened.
